items.title: Delegations
Warren Zeigler, President and Amy Gilbert, Vice President Elora
notes: Meadows Neighbourhood Group

Re: Item 8.3 Elora Meadows Neighbourhood Multi-Use Pad Project Warren Zeigler, President, Elora Meadows Community Association gave a presentation indicating in 2020, their community group built a small hockey rink for the community at the Elora Meadows park. In 2021, they were able to increase the size of the rink through fundraising efforts and coordinated efforts with the Township. Their proposal is to install a 70 x 130 pad to accommodate a 60 x 120 rink size and incorporate basketball nets and benches. The proposed design includes a fence to protect the neighbouring property. The space can also be used for rollerblades, pickleball, etc.
Mr. Zeigler provided clarification on pads proximity to neighbouring homes and the height of fencing and boards and noted the goal to raise $200 000.

items.title: Ian Rankine, resident spoke to item 8.2, Community Land Needs Review.
notes: He referenced the Heritage Landscapes Study currently in progress and spoke in support of the recommendation. He noted it is an opportunity for citizens to respond on where and how to grow. He raised concerns with the planning public meetings scheduled for February 22 for zoning amendments regarding building height and believes an Official Plan Amendment should be also be required.

items.title: Consideration of Reports
Planning and Development Fee Study
notes: Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development introduced Peter Simcisko, Watson and Associates. Mr. Salmon indicated the last planning fee review was completed in 2004, and in the previous term of Council a building fee analysis was presented and updated. The goal is to produce a fee structure that will result in full cost recovery. He informed Council the current fee structure from 2004 was set at 75% cost recovery at the time as per Council’s direction and staff is recommending shifting to 100% cost recovery.

Peter Simcisko, Watson and Associates gave a presentation outlining the objective of the Comprehensive Development Application Fees Review with regard for conformity with legislation, make if defensible, to balance the Township’s need to maximize cost recovery with stakeholder interests, affordability and competitiveness and follow industry best practices. He reviewed the activity-based costing methodology including direct costs, indirect costs and capital costs. The result of the study will be a fee recommendation coming back to Council.

items.title: Community Land Needs Review
notes: Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development Sarah Wilhelm, Manager of Policy Planning, County of Wellington gave a presentation regarding the land needs assessment for the County of Wellington as a whole. She reviewed the growth plan from the Province for the growth plan for the Greater Golden Horseshoe, indicating the County is part of the outer ring. She indicated a major change in the legislation is growth now being defined as a minimum instead of a maximum and an increase share of predicted growth has been assigned to the County of Wellington.
Councillor MacDonald raised concerns about the services available in Centre Wellington, such as daycare which are required to support growth.
In response to a question, Ms. Wilhelm explained the methodology for calculating intensification rates throughout the County.

Brett Salmon, Managing Director of Planning & Development, outlined the report and indicated staff would like to complete this study to look at the options to mitigate land needed for growth options and present all options to Council; however, he pointed out all land outside the existing urban boundary is agricultural.
Councillor Wilton requested this scenario be added to the recommendations to include the scenario with 30% intensification with 55% density in the Community Land Needs Review study.
